subject: Temporary priority window & SLO appendix request - Catalyzer onboarding
messages:
From: Claire Novak <claire@catalyzer.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Catalyzer Ops <ops@catalyzer.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:20:00 +0000
Subject: Request: temporary grace window for rate policy during onboarding

Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. We started our integration smoke tests yesterday and ran into heavy throttling from Redwood's fairness policy during concurrent connector runs. The traffic pattern is spiky because our QA harness replays dozens of user sessions in parallel for the first 36 hours of a rollout.

Can Catalyzer request a short-term carveout or credit window so the onboarding batch completes without hitting hard throttles? Specifically:
- Expected burst: ~6k req/min for ~6 hours (peak)
- Average token size: 1.2k
- Estimated total tokens over 48h: ~4.5M

What we need from Redwood: a temporary priority/burst pool or relaxed fairness weight for the onboarding window, and a short SLO appendix or note we can attach to procurement so procurement team can approve the go-live. We're happy to sign a short DocuSign amendment if needed.

I've attached a traffic snapshot from our QA run (integration-traffic-snapshot.csv).

Thanks — please loop in whoever owns the temporary rate/priority config.

—Claire
Claire Novak
Head of Integrations, Catalyzer
claire@catalyzer.com

---
Attachment: integration-traffic-snapshot.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Claire Novak <claire@catalyzer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary grace window for rate policy during onboarding

Claire — thanks for the traffic snapshot and the clear numbers. We can help here. Two implementation options we typically offer for onboarding spikes:

1) Temporary priority_token_pool (one-off allocation) — reserve an isolated token/burst pool for the window. Pro: minimal impact to fairness of other customers. Con: requires ops approval and quota adjustment.

2) Soft-fairness-weight bump — increase fairness weight for your tenant for a 48–72 hour window. Pro: quick to enable. Con: may affect short-term fairness for colocated tenants.

Operational constraints: we want to avoid changing contractual uptime SLA; this is an operational carveout that we document in an SLO appendix. We can provide a one-time incident credit if any throttling still causes partial failure for your critical flows.

Practical ask from us: can you confirm the expected start date/time (UTC), the absolute largest sustained RPS you expect, and whether the spike is read-only or includes embeddings/long-response generations? That will determine the model routing and kernel selection.

Proposed next steps:
- Monica / Marissa: can you review and suggest a config (priority pool size + soft-throttle thresholds)?
- Claire: if you confirm start window we’ll queue a SUP ticket and generate an SLO appendix draft for signature.

I attached a short draft SLO appendix template we can fill (slo-appendix-draft.docx).

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
---
Attachment: slo-appendix-draft.docx (docx, 18KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Novak <claire@catalyzer.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary grace window for rate policy during onboarding

Ben / Marissa / Claire — looping in operations details. Based on Claire's snapshot and Ben's options, my ops proposal: 

- Provision priority_token_pool = 2500000 tokens for a 72-hour window starting on 2027-05-28T00:00:00Z (UTC).
- Set soft-throttle to trigger at 95th percentile per-client token/sec; hard throttle remains unchanged but will fallback to a lower-cap model variant if sustainable throughput is exceeded.
- Routing: prefer gpt-3x-large-family variants for high-response workloads, embeddings routed to dedicated embedding pods.
- Monitoring: Redwood will enable token and latency tracing for the tenant and assign a runbook. We'll also open Jira SUP-3241 to capture the config steps and rollback criteria.

Notes about contractual language: this is an operational carveout — we can generate an SLO appendix that states: "For a one-time 72-hour priority window beginning at the mutually agreed start time, Redwood will allocate a priority token pool of X tokens and implement the described soft-throttle policy; this does not modify the baseline SLA for uptime but Redwood will provide a service credit for any qualified degradation arising from misrouting or infra failures during the window."

If that language sounds OK, I will:
- Create SUP-3241 and attach the final numbers,
- Draft the DocuSign amendment with the appendix (link to follow),
- Schedule a brief 15-min ops handoff for the start time.

Claire — can you confirm acceptance and the target start time? Also confirm the models you plan to use (generation vs embeddings).

Monica Patel
Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

---
Referenced: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3241

From: Claire Novak <claire@catalyzer.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: temporary grace window for rate policy during onboarding

Monica / Ben — appreciate the quick turnaround. Catalyzer accepts the proposal. Confirming:
- Start: 2027-05-28T00:00:00Z (UTC)
- Window: 72 hours
- Priority pool: 2,500,000 tokens
- Models: mix of generation (gpt-3x-large-family) and embeddings (embedding-v2).

Please proceed to create the SUP ticket and the DocuSign amendment. Procurement needs the final SLO appendix text to attach to the PO; if you can send the one-paragraph appendix today that would unblock us.

Thanks all — looking forward to the handoff.

—Claire
Claire Novak
Head of Integrations, Catalyzer
claire@catalyzer.com
